title: Path-versioned contract with announced deprecation and a stated drop policy
asA: API consumer maintaining a long-lived integration
iWant: the contract version visible in every URL and version retirement announced on the wire
soThat: I can plan migrations from response headers instead of discovering breakage in production

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every business endpoint lives under a major-version path prefix (/v1/...); only the probe endpoints and the documentation endpoints sit outside it.
acceptanceCriteria.when: paths are checked for the version prefix
acceptanceCriteria.then: every path is version-prefixed except /healthz/*, /openapi.*, and /docs

acceptanceCriteria.description: A request to an unrecognised major version returns 404 with a problem-details body naming the supported versions.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a request to /v9/ where v9 does not exist
acceptanceCriteria.then: the service responds 404 with the declared error envelope listing supported versions

acceptanceCriteria.description: Breaking changes never land inside an existing major version; additive changes (new fields, new endpoints) are the only in-version evolution.
acceptanceCriteria.given: two releases of the service within one major version
acceptanceCriteria.then: no field is removed or retyped and no endpoint's contract narrows within the version

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every response from a deprecated version carries Deprecation and Sunset headers with the retirement date.
acceptanceCriteria.then: Deprecation and Sunset headers are present and the Sunset date matches the declared policy

acceptanceCriteria.description: The version-drop policy is stated in the served documentation: minimum notice period and the response clients receive after drop (410 with a problem-details body pointing at the successor version).
acceptanceCriteria.given: the served documentation and a dropped version
acceptanceCriteria.when: a request reaches a dropped version
acceptanceCriteria.then: the service responds 410 with the declared error envelope naming the successor, matching the documented policy
